opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body: “Now this is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and the one whom you sent, Jesus Christ.” This is powerful because eternal life is not spoken of only as something waiting for us after death, but as something that begins now. We who love God and Jesus are already living eternal life even while we remain here on earth waiting for its fullness. Christ does not say eternal life will begin later. He says eternal life is to know the Father and to know Him. Through this relationship, something eternal is already planted within the soul. Our bodies will die, but our souls will carry on because death is no longer the final separation it once was. Christianity holds this mystery together: we are already participating in eternal life, yet we still await its fulfillment. It is the feeling that eternity has already broken into time. Through Christ, death becomes not an ending, but a passage. The body returns to dust for a time, but the soul continues toward the fullness of communion with God.”
